passage:
Zainab: I topped round 1 of the maths olympiad!!
Himani: WHAT 🎉
Zainab: I was about to post "some people should just quit maths"
Zainab: then I stopped
Himani: ...about Kiran?
Zainab: yeah. that's not pride, is it. that's needing her to be below me
Himani: kinda
Zainab: ok new post: "Topped round 1! Kiran's geometry solution was cleaner than mine, honestly"
Himani: that's true btw, ma'am said so
Zainab: ugh yes she did. fine. it WAS cleaner
Himani: see, you can be proud and still say that
Zainab: also ma'am said my proof skipped a step. fixed it tonight
Himani: proud of you for real
Zainab: me too. a bit

qa.q: Which round of the maths olympiad did Zainab top?
qa.a: Zainab topped round 1 of the maths olympiad.

qa.q: What did Zainab realise about the post Zainab almost wrote?
qa.a: Zainab realised it wasn't pride but a need for Kiran to be below, and chose not to post it.

qa.q: What choice did Zainab make instead of the mocking post, and why is it better?
qa.a: Zainab posted the win while praising Kiran's cleaner solution, showing pride that includes others.

qa.q: How might Kiran feel reading the new post?
qa.a: She would likely feel noticed and respected rather than put down.

grounding: In a chat, a teenager checks whether a win needs a rival pushed below, praises the rival instead and calmly fixes a corrected proof.

passage: At the taluka science exhibition in Sangamner, Anand's solar dryer for onions won first place. Back in the village, the men at the tea stall slapped his back, and his cousin said, "Now go tell Ganesh his windmill was rubbish." Anand almost laughed along. Then he pictured Ganesh's face at the exhibition and stopped. Did his prize only feel big if Ganesh felt small? "His windmill actually turned," he said. "Mine won because of the chart." The next day Parul ma'am pointed out a mistake in his temperature readings. His ears burned. "Show me where," he said, and fixed the numbers that evening by lantern light, still proud of his dryer.

qa.q: What did Anand's project dry?
qa.a: It was a solar dryer for onions.

qa.q: What made Anand stop laughing along with his cousin?
qa.a: He pictured Ganesh's face and asked himself whether his prize only felt big if Ganesh felt small, and he didn't want that.

qa.q: How did Anand handle Parul ma'am's correction, and why was it wise?
qa.a: His ears burned, but he asked her to show him and fixed the numbers that evening, accepting the correction without losing his pride.

qa.q: How might Ganesh feel if he heard Anand praise his windmill?
qa.a: He would probably feel respected and less bruised by losing.

grounding: A village teenager checks whether his pride needs others below him, praises a rival and accepts a teacher's correction without collapse.

passage: Camila's robotics team in Valencia won the regional prize, and at lunch she heard herself say, "Honestly, I did most of the coding. Hana just did the wiring." Hana stopped eating. That night Camila couldn't sleep. She asked herself: am I proud because we built something good, or because I need to be the best one? The next morning she found Hana by the lockers. "What I said was unfair. Your wiring is why it didn't short out. We both did well." Hana crossed her arms, then pointed out that Camila's code had also crashed twice. Camila flushed, then laughed. "True. Fix it together for nationals?"

qa.q: Where did Camila find Hana the next morning?
qa.a: By the lockers.

qa.q: What was Camila feeling the night after the lunch comment?
qa.a: She felt uneasy and guilty, unable to sleep while questioning her pride.

qa.q: What did Camila do that shows real pride?
qa.a: She apologised, credited Hana's work and accepted Hana's correction about the code without collapsing.

qa.q: How did Hana feel when Camila dismissed the wiring?
qa.a: Hana was hurt, stopping eating, and later stood up for herself by pointing out the crashes.

grounding: Shows a teen asking whether her pride needs others below, then crediting a teammate and accepting correction.

passage: At the chess club in the community centre, Madhav had just beaten three players in a row and was telling the juniors, loudly, how easy it had been. Coach Rajni pulled up a chair. "Show me your endgame against Keya. You nearly lost that one. Here, and here." Madhav felt the old heat rise, the urge to say the coach was wrong. He stopped. Lately he'd been thinking about the difference between feeling good about his game and needing everyone else to feel small. "You're right," he said. "I got lucky there." Then he turned to Keya. "You played the middle game better than me. Want to go over it together?" Keya's eyes widened. Coach Rajni smiled and moved on to the next table.

qa.q: How many players had Madhav beaten in a row?
qa.a: Three players.

qa.q: What was Madhav feeling when Coach Rajni pointed out his mistakes?
qa.a: He felt a flash of defensive anger, then chose to calm it and accept the correction.

qa.q: What question does Madhav seem to ask himself, and why does it matter?
qa.a: Whether his pride needs others to feel small; asking it lets him admit luck and praise Keya.

qa.q: How might Keya feel when Madhav offers to go over the game?
qa.a: Keya is surprised and pleased, being praised by the player who just beat her.

grounding: Illustrates a teen noticing the pull of arrogance, accepting correction and sharing credit with another player.

passage:
Simran,
After the results came out, I said something at the bus stop I've been thinking about all week: "Some of us actually study." You'd got 71 in chemistry, I'd got 94, and I wanted everyone to know it. I've been asking myself why. I am proud of that 94. I worked for it, and I'm allowed to be glad. But I noticed I only felt really good when someone else looked worse. That's not pride; it's something else. You also told me my physics diagram was copied from a website. I was angry, but you were right. I've redone it. You did well in biology, better than me. I should have said so.
Tushar

qa.q: What did Tushar score in chemistry?
What did Tushar notice about that good feeling?
qa.a: Tushar noticed that feeling really good came only when someone else looked worse, and felt uneasy about that kind of pride.

qa.q: What shows that Tushar accepted correction without collapse?
qa.a: Tushar admitted Simran was right about the copied diagram and redid it.

qa.q: How might Simran feel reading this letter?
qa.a: Simran may feel respected and relieved after the bus-stop remark, seeing Tushar credit the biology result.

grounding: Shows a teen asking whether pride needs others below, accepting correction and naming another's success.

passage:
Preeti, you know what I asked myself after the science fair? I'm Lalit, the one who came second, and I want to tell you honestly.
When they said my water filter was second and yours was first, part of me wanted to say yours was simple. I felt that ugly flash. So I asked myself: does my pride need you below me?
And the answer was, it shouldn't. My filter worked. I did well. And your solar dryer was genuinely clever. You did well too. Both things are true.
Then the judge said my data table had errors. Old me would have argued, or sulked for a week. I felt my face go hot, but I said, "Can you show me where?" She did. She was right.
So now I'm fixing the table. And I want to see how you built the dryer lid.

qa.q: What did Preeti build for the science fair?
qa.a: A solar dryer.

qa.q: How did Lalit feel when Preeti won first place?
qa.a: Lalit felt a flash of envy and wanted to call Preeti's project simple, but stopped to ask whether that pride needed Preeti below.

qa.q: How did Lalit handle the judge's correction wisely?
qa.a: Lalit felt embarrassed but asked, "Can you show me where?", listened, accepted the judge was right and started fixing the table.

qa.q: How might Preeti feel hearing Lalit say Preeti did well too?
qa.a: Preeti would probably feel respected and glad, especially when Lalit asks to see how the dryer lid was built.

grounding: Shows a teen checking whether their pride needs others below, crediting a rival's work and accepting correction without collapse.
